angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 193,057 km at 64.62 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.4752 +/- 0.0345 mas (same row, RUWE 1.12): 64.62 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.2775 +/- 0.008 solar radii from Mori et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1696 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..298M/abstract): 193,057 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.255 +/- 0.0066 solar masses from Mori et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1696 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..298M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3185 +/- 76 K from Mori et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1696 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..298M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mori et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1696 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163..298M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1696.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.958, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
